title: Regulated Sector Schema
description: A regulated sector within a jurisdiction, such as banking or superannuation in Australia: the field an organization works in, grouping the entity types obligations are addressed to. Apps let a user choose a jurisdiction, then a sector, then the entity type, and use the sector to scope obligations and engagements. A sector describes who sources address, not which law binds a particular organization; that is for counsel.

regulatedSectorID.description: Unique identifier for the sector: the jurisdiction code and a short name, e.g. AU-BANKING

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction the sector belongs to, e.g. AU

name.description: Short name shown to users, e.g. Banking

description.description: What the sector covers, in plain words

financiallyRegulated.description: True when a prudential or financial services regulator licenses the entities in the sector. Apps use it to suggest a connected engagement; it is not a finding about any organization

regulators.description: Short names of the regulators most associated with the sector, for display

entityTypes.description: Entity types an organization in the sector chooses from

alsoReaches.description: Broader entity types whose sources also reach an organization in the sector, such as financialInstitution for every MAS-licensed sector. Records addressed to anyOrganization reach every sector and are not listed

mainSector.description: True for one of the jurisdiction's main sectors (at most five a jurisdiction): a sector with its own Atlas records, a sector pack in each engagement app and a worked example. Other sectors stay selectable and use their baseline or the general path

baselineProfiles.description: Baseline profiles (baseline-profiles.json) the sector builds on; the sector's own obligations are the jurisdiction's overlay on them
